Summary: Reverts the preceding CTTZ_ELTS[_ZERO_POISON] legalization refactoring. It removes TargetLowering::expandCttzElts and the vector split/promotion/expansion dispatches, then restores SelectionDAGBuilder's earlier conditional eager expansion based on shouldExpandCttzElements. It also restores the prior type construction in expandVectorFindLastActive.
Changed symbols: SelectionDAGBuilder::visitIntrinsicCall; TargetLowering::expandCttzElts; DAGTypeLegalizer::SplitVectorOperand; DAGTypeLegalizer::PromoteIntegerOperand; VectorLegalizer::LegalizeOp; VectorLegalizer::Expand; TargetLowering::expandVectorFindLastActive

top_candidates.subject: [SelectionDAG] Optimize 32-bit udiv with 33-bit magic constants on 64-bit targets (#181288)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This changes SelectionDAG unsigned-division construction in TargetLowering::BuildUDIV so that scalar i32 constant divisions may use a widened i64 magic-factor sequence on targets supporting legal or custom i64 MULHU or UMUL_LOHI. When the magic-divisor computation requests widening, the code zero-extends the i32 dividend to i64, performs a 64x64 high-half multiply using an i64 magic constant, and truncates the result back to i32; corresponding X86 code-generation tests are added and updated.
Changed symbols: TargetLowering::BuildUDIV
Behavioral change: Enables the magic-number division helper's widening optimization for non-vector 32-bit unsigned divisions when i64 high-half multiplication is legal or custom.; Changes selected DAG shape for eligible i32 udiv operations from same-width magic multiplication to ZERO_EXTEND(i32->i64), i64 MULHU or UMUL_LOHI, and TRUNCATE(i64->i32).; Uses the unextended i64 magic factor when the magic computation reports magics.Widen.
Assertion or trace link: SelectionDAG; integer width adjustment
Reproducer link: X86 x86_64 code generation is explicitly covered by new udiv constant-optimization tests.
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG TargetLowering; X86 code generation
Causal explanation: This is an indirect but plausible candidate because it introduces explicit integer widening, zero-extension, and truncation into SelectionDAGs later selected for X86, which is the class of width reasoning implicated by the low-bits-constraint assertion. The new X86_64 path can alter DAG patterns reaching X86 instruction selection. However, the retrieved hunks do not modify X86ISelLowering.cpp, peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, combineBTToBitOpFlag, bit-test lowering, or the asserted low-bits invariant, and the change is limited to constant unsigned division.
Causal confidence: 0.34
Build risk: The widened path is guarded by legality/custom-lowering checks for i64 MULHU and UMUL_LOHI.; New llc/FileCheck coverage exercises x86_64, x86_64 with BMI2, and i386 output for constant i32 unsigned division.; An existing X86 urem-loop test expectation changes because the new i64 magic-multiply sequence is selected.

+
+; Test optimization of 32-bit unsigned division by constants with 33-bit magic
+; constants (IsAdd=true) on 64-bit targets. The optimization uses pre-shifted
+; constants and 64x64->128 bit multiplication to reduce instruction count.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Changes SelectionDAG constant-division lowering to permit selected signed and unsigned division-by-constant transforms for vector types before type legalization, provided legalization retains the vector form and element type. BuildSDIV and BuildUDIV query multiply-high and multiply-low/high legality using a legal transformed query type, while DAGCombiner::visitMULHU permits its shift-related fold before legal operations are required.
Changed symbols: TargetLowering::BuildSDIV; TargetLowering::BuildUDIV; DAGCombiner::visitMULHU
Behavioral change: BuildSDIV and BuildUDIV use QueryVT, rather than the original VT, when querying legality of MULHS/MULHU and SMUL_LOHI/UMUL_LOHI.; For vector VTs before type legalization, division-by-constant lowering may proceed only when legalization produces another vector with the same element type; otherwise it returns no transform.; The fallback condition involving absent multiply-high support is restricted by isTypeLegal(VT).; DAGCombiner::visitMULHU may perform its SRL-dependent combine before legal-operations mode, rather than requiring hasOperation(ISD::SRL, VT) unconditionally.
Assertion or trace link: DAGCombiner; pre-type-legalization type and width reasoning; No retrieved hunk mentions peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, combineBTToBitOpFlag, the X86 low-bits constraint assertion, or X86ISelLowering.
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O1 X86 SelectionDAG instruction-selection crash.; This change can alter pre-legalization DAG shapes at optimization levels using DAG combining, but the retrieved evidence does not show that the reproducer contains division by a constant, MULHU, or an odd-sized vector.
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG DAGCombiner; TargetLowering constant-division expansion; pre-type-legalization vector handling
Causal explanation: This is the closest candidate to the reported subsystem because it directly changes DAGCombiner behavior and target legality decisions before type legalization. New multiply-high, shift, and division expansion DAG shapes could theoretically reach later X86 combines with different width information. Still, the change is narrowly conditioned on constant division and, for the newly enabled case, vectors whose element type survives legalization; it neither changes the X86 BT-to-bit-op combine nor references the low-bits invariant. The evidence supports a possible but indirect connection.

steps.subject: [DAGCombiner] Teach `reduceLoadWidth` to look past `ISD:FREEZE` (#189317)

evidence: Introduces DAGCombiner width reduction through FREEZE and explicitly creates AssertZext/AssertSext to preserve range and low-bit facts.
Directly overlaps the reported low-bits-constraint-survives-width-adjustment assertion and has dedicated X86 mask/truncation/extension coverage.
features: assertzext-assertsext, dagcombiner, low-bits-constraint, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/CodeGen/SelectionDAG, path:llvm/test/CodeGen/AArch64
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends SelectionDAG load-width reduction through an intervening ISD::FREEZE. DAGCombiner::visitAND now recognizes a freeze-wrapped load as eligible for reduceLoadWidth, while DAGCombiner::reduceLoadWidth preserves the freeze around the narrowed result, emits AssertZext or AssertSext to retain extension-range information, and constrains multi-use-freeze rewrites so dependent users cannot incorrectly observe a narrowed value.
Changed symbols: DAGCombiner::visitAND; DAGCombiner::reduceLoadWidth; ISD::FREEZE; ISD::AssertZext; ISD::AssertSext; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/reduce-load-width-freeze.ll; and_freeze_load_i32_to_i8; and_freeze_load_i64_to_i8
Behavioral change: visitAND may now invoke reduceLoadWidth for an AND whose non-constant operand is FREEZE(LOAD), rather than requiring the operand itself to be a LOAD.; reduceLoadWidth explicitly looks through ISD::FREEZE and rewraps the reduced result in a freeze.; After narrowing a freeze-wrapped zextload or sextload, the combiner creates ISD::AssertZext or ISD::AssertSext carrying the narrowed extension width so downstream DAG analyses retain the value-range constraint.; For a multi-use freeze, reduction is rejected when narrowing would change a full-width value observed by another user, except for the safe anyext-to-zext case described by the added guard.; For an allowed multi-use freeze rewrite, uses of the old frozen value are redirected to the new load result.
Assertion or trace link: SelectionDAG; DAGCombiner; low bits constraint; width adjustment; AssertZext; AssertSext
Reproducer link: The added X86 tests directly cover low-bit masking, truncation, zero extension, and sign extension through freeze-wrapped loads.; The reported crash is in X86 DAG instruction selection and concerns preservation of a low-bits constraint across width adjustment; this commit introduces exactly such width-reduction and range-assertion propagation in SelectionDAG.
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG DAGCombiner; DAGCombiner::visitAND; DAGCombiner::reduceLoadWidth; X86 SelectionDAG code generation
Causal explanation: This is a strong bisect candidate because it changes generic DAG-combine behavior for low-bit masks and truncation-like width reduction, and it adds AssertZext/AssertSext nodes specifically to preserve extension/range facts after narrowing. Those facts are plausibly consumed by later X86 DAG combines and match the issue's low-bits-constraint/width-adjustment theme. The retrieved hunks do not name peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc or combineBTToBitOpFlag, so a direct causal path to the exact assertion is not proven, but the subsystem and invariant overlap are substantial.
Causal confidence: 0.74

Summary: This commit extends SelectionDAG load-width reduction through an intervening ISD::FREEZE. DAGCombiner::visitAND now recognizes a freeze-wrapped load as eligible for reduceLoadWidth, while DAGCombiner::reduceLoadWidth preserves the freeze around the narrowed result, emits AssertZext or AssertSext to retain extension-range information, and constrains multi-use-freeze rewrites so dependent users cannot incorrectly observe a narrowed value.
Changed symbols: DAGCombiner::visitAND; DAGCombiner::reduceLoadWidth; ISD::FREEZE; ISD::AssertZext; ISD::AssertSext; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/reduce-load-width-freeze.ll; and_freeze_load_i32_to_i8; and_freeze_load_i64_to_i8
Behavioral change: visitAND may now invoke reduceLoadWidth for an AND whose non-constant operand is FREEZE(LOAD), rather than requiring the operand itself to be a LOAD.; reduceLoadWidth explicitly looks through ISD::FREEZE and rewraps the reduced result in a freeze.; After narrowing a freeze-wrapped zextload or sextload, the combiner creates ISD::AssertZext or ISD::AssertSext carrying the narrowed extension width so downstream DAG analyses retain the value-range constraint.; For a multi-use freeze, reduction is rejected when narrowing would change a full-width value observed by another user, except for the safe anyext-to-zext case described by the added guard.; For an allowed multi-use freeze rewrite, uses of the old frozen value are redirected to the new load result.
Assertion or trace link: SelectionDAG; DAGCombiner; low bits constraint; width adjustment; AssertZext; AssertSext
Reproducer link: The added X86 tests directly cover low-bit masking, truncation, zero extension, and sign extension through freeze-wrapped loads.; The reported crash is in X86 DAG instruction selection and concerns preservation of a low-bits constraint across width adjustment; this commit introduces exactly such width-reduction and range-assertion propagation in SelectionDAG.
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG DAGCombiner; DAGCombiner::visitAND; DAGCombiner::reduceLoadWidth; X86 SelectionDAG code generation
Causal explanation: This is a strong bisect candidate because it changes generic DAG-combine behavior for low-bit masks and truncation-like width reduction, and it adds AssertZext/AssertSext nodes specifically to preserve extension/range facts after narrowing. Those facts are plausibly consumed by later X86 DAG combines and match the issue's low-bits-constraint/width-adjustment theme. The retrieved hunks do not name peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc or combineBTToBitOpFlag, so a direct causal path to the exact assertion is not proven, but the subsystem and invariant overlap are substantial.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Changes SelectionDAG expansion of signed-subtract-with-overflow (SSUBO). Instead of computing overflow from (Result < LHS) XOR (RHS > 0), the subtraction path now computes it as (LHS < RHS) XOR (Result < 0), while retaining the existing addition predicate. X86 vector SSUBO code-generation expectations are updated for SSE, AVX, and AVX-512.
Changed symbols: TargetLowering::expandSADDSUBO; DAGTypeLegalizer::ExpandIntRes_SADDSUBO; ssubo_v2i32; ssubo_v3i32; ssubo_v4i32; ssubo_v6i32
Behavioral change: The SSUBO subtraction-overflow predicate changes from comparing the result against LHS plus checking whether RHS is positive to comparing LHS against RHS plus checking whether the subtraction result is negative.; The subtraction expansion now constructs SETLT nodes for LHS < RHS and Result < 0, XORs those boolean values, and extends or truncates the result to the intrinsic overflow-result type.; The changed DAG shape produces different X86 vector compare, subtraction, zeroing, and XOR instruction sequences.

top_candidates.subject: [SelectionDAG] Use Magic Algorithm for Splitting UDIV/UREM by Constant (#154968)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit replaces the prior unsigned constant div/rem splitting path with a new magic-number-based expansion for UDIV, UREM, and UDIVREM. The implementation computes unsigned-division magic parameters using known leading-zero information, performs widened pair arithmetic with UMUL_LOHI, carry-aware add/subtract, and split shifts, and uses the computed quotient to reconstruct a remainder when required. Summary: This commit changes only X86 masked integer division/remainder test coverage. It replaces feature-flag test invocations with x86-64 CPU-level invocations for SSE/SSE4.2/AVX2/AVX-512, and adds SSE4.2 and AVX2 assembly checks for masked <2 x i128> signed and unsigned division and remainder lowering.
Changed symbols: sdiv_v2i128; srem_v2i128; udiv_v2i128; urem_v2i128; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/masked-sdiv.ll RUN lines; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/masked-srem.ll RUN lines; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/masked-udiv.ll RUN lines; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/masked-urem.ll RUN lines

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Changes X86ISelLowering::LowerBUILD_VECTORvXi1 to recognize BUILD_VECTOR masks with more than one nonconstant i8-derived element and lower them through a byte-vector BUILD_VECTOR, an ANY_EXTEND to an i8- or i32-element vector depending on BWI support, an AND with 1, and a SETCC-not-equal-zero result. This creates a new vector boolean-mask lowering route intended to enable VPTESTMB-style folding.
Changed symbols: X86ISelLowering::LowerBUILD_VECTORvXi1; test_maskz_store_v192i8
Behavioral change: Introduces a new lowering path for multiple nonconstant i8 inputs used to form a vXi1 BUILD_VECTOR.; Constructs a byte BUILD_VECTOR, widens it with ISD::ANY_EXTEND, masks every widened lane with 1, and converts the nonzero result back to the requested boolean vector with ISD::SETCC.; Selects the intermediate widened element type as i8 with BWI and i32 without BWI.; Updates the AVX-512 masked-store FileCheck expectations, showing that this lowering materially changes generated code for a large <192 x i1> mask case.
Assertion or trace link: llvm/lib/Target/X86/X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG; No retrieved hunk directly changes peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc or combineBTToBitOpFlag.
Reproducer link: The new path specifically handles nonconstant <N x i1> BUILD_VECTOR masks sourced from i8 values.; The retrieved candidate test update affects an AVX-512 <192 x i1> masked-store case.; The supplied reduced C -O1 reproducer shape is not present in the retrieved hunks, so direct input-pattern equivalence is unproven.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 SelectionDAG lowering; LowerBUILD_VECTORvXi1; Downstream X86 DAG combines consuming ANY_EXTEND, AND, and SETCC nodes
Causal explanation: This is a plausible cause because it introduces a fresh width-changing boolean-mask DAG pattern in the exact X86 lowering area named by the issue. In particular, ANY_EXTEND followed by low-bit masking can expose values to later bit-test or demanded-bits combines whose assertion requires low-bit constraints to survive a width adjustment. The evidence is indirect: the candidate does not modify the asserted helper or the BT combine itself, and the retrieved material does not establish that the C reproducer reaches this BUILD_VECTOR path.
Causal confidence: 0.48
Build risk: Touches target-specific X86 SelectionDAG lowering rather than an isolated test or documentation path.; The new route is feature-sensitive through Subtarget.hasBWI() and changes intermediate vector element widths.; A candidate-owned AVX-512 code-generation test expectation is updated, but no test for the reported assertion or C -O1 crash is visible.; Retrieved diff coverage is truncated, so only the shown lowering and test effects can be assessed.

Summary: Changes X86ISelLowering::LowerBUILD_VECTORvXi1 to recognize BUILD_VECTOR masks with more than one nonconstant i8-derived element and lower them through a byte-vector BUILD_VECTOR, an ANY_EXTEND to an i8- or i32-element vector depending on BWI support, an AND with 1, and a SETCC-not-equal-zero result. This creates a new vector boolean-mask lowering route intended to enable VPTESTMB-style folding.
Changed symbols: X86ISelLowering::LowerBUILD_VECTORvXi1; test_maskz_store_v192i8
Behavioral change: Introduces a new lowering path for multiple nonconstant i8 inputs used to form a vXi1 BUILD_VECTOR.; Constructs a byte BUILD_VECTOR, widens it with ISD::ANY_EXTEND, masks every widened lane with 1, and converts the nonzero result back to the requested boolean vector with ISD::SETCC.; Selects the intermediate widened element type as i8 with BWI and i32 without BWI.; Updates the AVX-512 masked-store FileCheck expectations, showing that this lowering materially changes generated code for a large <192 x i1> mask case.
Assertion or trace link: llvm/lib/Target/X86/X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG; No retrieved hunk directly changes peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc or combineBTToBitOpFlag.

Pass or subsystem link: X86 SelectionDAG lowering; LowerBUILD_VECTORvXi1; Downstream X86 DAG combines consuming ANY_EXTEND, AND, and SETCC nodes

In particular, ANY_EXTEND followed by low-bit masking can expose values to later bit-test or demanded-bits combines whose assertion requires low-bit constraints to survive a width adjustment. selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Reworks X86 SelectionDAG lowering of BUILD_VECTOR vectors of i1 so that vectors containing one distinct non-constant element are scalarized through a select between computed bit masks. It replaces non-constant-index/splat tracking with a bit mask plus a set of distinct non-constant SDValues, constructs true and false immediates for the selected mask, adjusts an all-ones extended true value to the destination integer width, and inserts dynamic elements according to the mask.
Changed symbols: LowerBUILD_VECTORvXi1
Behavioral change: Changes the scalarization eligibility test from an all-elements splat condition to the presence of exactly one distinct non-constant element.; Tracks positions of non-constant BUILD_VECTOR operands in NonConstMask and tracks distinct non-constant SDValues in NonConstElts.; Builds select true and false integer mask values from NonConstMask and Immediate rather than always selecting all-ones versus zero.; Adjusts a true mask to an all-ones value at ImmVT width when the resulting vector-width mask, accounting for Undefs, is all ones.; For v64i1, emits separate low and high i32 selects and concatenates their bitcasts; otherwise it emits a select at ImmVT.; Reinserts non-constant vector elements according to NonConstMask using DAG.getInsertVectorElt.
Assertion or trace link: X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG; integer width adjustment
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O1 X86 backend assertion during SelectionDAG combining; this change can create different i1 vector mask/select DAG shapes and integer-width constants before those combines.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 SelectionDAG lowering; SelectionDAG combine input formation; boolean-mask and bit-vector lowering

Those altered DAG forms could plausibly reach bit-test or extension/truncation combines implicated by the low-bits assertion. Summary: Extends the X86 DAG combine for GF2P8AFFINEQB XOR patterns. In addition to folding an affine result XORed with a constant splat, combineXorWithGF2P8AFFINEQB now recognizes GF2P8AFFINEQB(x, M) XOR x, folds the XOR into the affine matrix by XORing identity-matrix rows, and emits a replacement GF2P8AFFINEQB node. New X86 GFNI tests cover 128-, 256-, and 512-bit cases, constant and nonzero-immediate matrices, and cases that must not fold.
Changed symbols: combineXorWithGF2P8AFFINEQB; test_affine_src_xor_fold_128; test_affine_src_xor_fold_256; test_affine_src_xor_fold_512; test_affine_src_xor_fold_alternative_matrix; test_affine_src_xor_nonzero_imm; test_affine_src_xor_no_fold_multi_use; test_affine_src_xor_no_fold_var_matrix

diff --git a/llvm/docs/AMDGPUUsage.rst b/llvm/docs/AMDGPUUsage.rst
index 8dd743a995a9..61841716792e 100644
--- a/llvm/docs/AMDGPUUsage.rst
+++ b/llvm/docs/AMDGPUUsage.rst
@@ -832,0 +833,49 @@ For example:
+.. _amdgpu-module-flags:
+
+Module Flags
+------------
+
+AMDGPU-specific behaviour can be controlled via LLVM module flags (see
+`Module Flags Metadata
+<https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#module-flags-metadata>`_ in the language
+reference). These flags are set by frontends and are
+consumed by the AMDGPU backend during code generation.
+
+.. list-table:: AMDGPU Module Flags
+   :name: amdgpu-module-flags-table
+   :header-rows: 1
+
+   * - Flag Name
+     - Type
+     - Merge
+     - Description
+   * - ``amdgpu.buffer.oob.mode``
+     - ``i32``
+     - Max
+     - Controls out-of-bounds semantics for untyped buffer
+       instructions (``buffer_load`` / ``buffer_store``).
+
+       - ``0`` (or absent): **any**. The module does not care about OOB
+         semantics. This is an alias of **strict** that is allowed to link
+         with any other module. Code generation is identical to **strict**.
+       - ``1``: **relaxed**. The backend may merge misaligned buffer
+         accesses for performance, even if that changes OOB behaviour.
+       - ``2``: **strict**. The backend preserves per-byte OOB guarantees
+         by preventing merging of misaligned buffer accesses that could
+         straddle an OOB boundary (e.g. as required by Vulkan
+         ``robustBufferAccess2``).
+
+   * - ``amdgpu.tbuffer.oob.mode``
+     - ``i32``
+     - Max
+     - Same as above, but for typed buffer instructions (``tbuffer_load`` /
+       ``tbuffer_store``).
+
+.. note::
+
+   Frontends that require misaligned-access merging for performance should
+   set both flags to ``1`` (relaxed).  Frontends that require strict
+   per-byte OOB guarantees should set the flags to ``2`` (strict) as needed.
+   Modules that do not use buffer operations or are indifferent to OOB semantics
+   (e.g. device libraries) should leave the flags absent.
+

+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+//
+// Part of the LLVM Project, under the Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions.

+///
+/// \file
+/// This file contains the declaration of the BreakFalseDepsPass class, used to
+/// identify and avoid false dependencies which cause unnecessary stalls.
+///
+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+
+#ifndef LLVM_CODEGEN_BREAKFALSEDEPS_H
+#define LLVM_CODEGEN_BREAKFALSEDEPS_H
+
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/MachineFunction.h"
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/MachineFunctionAnalysisManager.h"
+#include "llvm/IR/PassManager.h"
+#include "llvm/Support/Compiler.h"
+
+namespace llvm {
+
+class BreakFalseDepsPass : public PassInfoMixin<BreakFalseDepsPass> {
+public:
+  LLVM_ABI PreservedAnalyses run(MachineFunction &MF,
+                                 MachineFunctionAnalysisManager &MFAM);
+
+  MachineFunctionProperties getRequiredProperties() const {
+    return MachineFunctionProperties().setNoVRegs();
+  }
+};
+
+} // namespace llvm
+

top_candidates.subject: [SelectionDAG] Widen <2 x T> vector types for atomic store (#197618)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This candidate adds SelectionDAG vector-type legalization support for atomic stores whose vector operands must be widened, particularly <2 x T>-style cases. It selects an atomic memory type of the original width, coerces the widened store value back to that type through a bitcast/extract sequence when needed, and emits a replacement ATOMIC_STORE; X86 tests cover atomic vector stores of several element widths and pointer types.
Changed symbols: coerceStoredValue; DAGTypeLegalizer::WidenVecOp_ATOMIC_STORE; DAGTypeLegalizer::WidenVectorOperand; DAGTypeLegalizer::WidenVecOp_ATOMIC_STORE declaration
Behavioral change: Routes ISD::ATOMIC_STORE through vector-operand widening legalization.; Finds a memory type matching the original atomic-store width rather than allowing alignment to widen the atomic access past the stored object.; Converts a widened scalar store value to a vector and extracts lane zero, or preserves an already matching vector value, before creating the replacement atomic store.; Adds X86 code-generation coverage for atomic stores of <2 x i8>, <2 x i16>, <2 x ptr addrspace(270)>, and related vector types.
Assertion or trace link: SelectionDAG; width adjustment
Reproducer link: The retrieved tests cover atomic vector-store lowering at O0 and O3, not the reported reduced C testcase or its -O1 assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG type legalization; X86 atomic-store instruction selection
Causal explanation: This is a plausible but indirect candidate because it changes SelectionDAG width-adjustment behavior, and the reported assertion explicitly concerns preservation of a low-bits constraint across a width adjustment. However, the changed path is narrowly for widened vector atomic stores and introduces bitcast/extract coercions for those stores; the retrieved hunks contain no bit-test, combineBTToBitOpFlag, peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, sign/zero-extension constraint, or direct X86 DAG-combine change. The available tests likewise establish atomic-store code generation rather than the reported O1 crash.
Causal confidence: 0.22
Build risk: The new legalization path must preserve atomic access width and memory-operand semantics while converting widened vector values.; The code relies on findMemType returning a valid original-width atomic memory type and returns an empty SDValue when it cannot.; The new scalar coercion uses a BITCAST to a constructed vector type followed by lane-zero extraction, creating a type-legalization-sensitive transformation.; Retrieved X86 tests provide coverage for atomic-store instruction sequences, but no regression test covers the reported low-bits assertion.

Summary: The candidate broadens X86 store-folding and instruction-selection patterns to accept atomic stores in addition to ordinary stores. X86::mayFoldIntoStore now treats ISD::ATOMIC_STORE as foldable, while several SSE and AVX-512 extract-to-memory patterns replace ordinary store predicates with any_store predicates so they may match atomic-store forms.

diff --git a/llvm/docs/AMDGPUUsage.rst b/llvm/docs/AMDGPUUsage.rst
index 8dd743a995a9..61841716792e 100644
--- a/llvm/docs/AMDGPUUsage.rst
+++ b/llvm/docs/AMDGPUUsage.rst
@@ -832,0 +833,49 @@ For example:
+.. _amdgpu-module-flags:
+
+Module Flags
+------------
+
+AMDGPU-specific behaviour can be controlled via LLVM module flags (see
+`Module Flags Metadata
+<https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#module-flags-metadata>`_ in the language
+reference). These flags are set by frontends and are
+consumed by the AMDGPU backend during code generation.
+
+.. list-table:: AMDGPU Module Flags
+   :name: amdgpu-module-flags-table
+   :header-rows: 1
+
+   * - Flag Name
+     - Type
+     - Merge
+     - Description
+   * - ``amdgpu.buffer.oob.mode``
+     - ``i32``
+     - Max
+     - Controls out-of-bounds semantics for untyped buffer
+       instructions (``buffer_load`` / ``buffer_store``).
+
+       - ``0`` (or absent): **any**. The module does not care about OOB
+         semantics. This is an alias of **strict** that is allowed to link
+         with any other module. Code generation is identical to **strict**.
+       - ``1``: **relaxed**. The backend may merge misaligned buffer
+         accesses for performance, even if that changes OOB behaviour.
+       - ``2``: **strict**. The backend preserves per-byte OOB guarantees
+         by preventing merging of misaligned buffer accesses that could
+         straddle an OOB boundary (e.g. as required by Vulkan
+         ``robustBufferAccess2``).
+
+   * - ``amdgpu.tbuffer.oob.mode``
+     - ``i32``
+     - Max
+     - Same as above, but for typed buffer instructions (``tbuffer_load`` /
+       ``tbuffer_store``).
+
+.. note::
+
+   Frontends that require misaligned-access merging for performance should
+   set both flags to ``1`` (relaxed).  Frontends that require strict
+   per-byte OOB guarantees should set the flags to ``2`` (strict) as needed.
+   Modules that do not use buffer operations or are indifferent to OOB semantics
+   (e.g. device libraries) should leave the flags absent.
+

Summary: This X86 SelectionDAG-combine change extends combineXorWithGF2P8AFFINEQB to recognize an XOR between a VGF2P8AFFINEQB result and that operation's original source. For a constant GFNI affine matrix, it folds the XOR into a replacement GF2P8AFFINEQB whose matrix rows are XORed with the byte identity matrix; it also renames the matched XOR operand from SplatOp to XorOp and retains the existing constant-splat folding path using that operand.
Changed symbols: combineXorWithGF2P8AFFINEQB; X86::isConstantSplat; getTargetConstantBitsFromNode
Behavioral change: Adds a fold from GF2P8AFFINEQB(x, M, Imm) ^ x to GF2P8AFFINEQB(x, M ^ IDENTITY, Imm) when the affine matrix can be extracted as constant 8-bit element values.; Builds a new vector matrix by XORing each extracted matrix row with the repeating identity rows {128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1}.; Uses XorOp, rather than the former SplatOp name, as the non-GFNI XOR operand for both source-XOR recognition and the existing constant-splat check.; Adds X86 GFNI tests for 128-, 256-, and 512-bit source-XOR folding, including non-splat matrices, nonzero immediates, multi-use no-fold cases, variable matrices, and unrelated-variable XOR no-fold cases.
Assertion or trace link: X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG combine logic
Reproducer link: The new tests exercise vector i8 GFNI affine operations followed by XOR, not the reduced C testcase or an -O1 scalar bit-test/extension pattern.; No retrieved hunk mentions 'low bits constraint must survive width adjustment', peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, or combineBTToBitOpFlag.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 SelectionDAG combining; X86ISelLowering
Causal explanation: This is the strongest subsystem match because it directly changes X86ISelLowering SelectionDAG combine behavior and performs constant-bit extraction plus construction of replacement DAG values. However, the changed transform is narrowly for GF2P8AFFINEQB vector-i8 affine operations and source XORs. The issue trace instead identifies bit-test lowering and width/extension reasoning in peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc and combineBTToBitOpFlag. The retrieved evidence does not establish that the reproducer contains GFNI operations or reaches this combiner, so the link is plausible only at the broad X86 DAG-combine level.
Causal confidence: 0.22
Build risk: Introduces new X86 DAG-combine code using APInt, SmallVector, getTargetConstantBitsFromNode, DAG.getBuildVector, and a replacement X86ISD::GF2P8AFFINEQB node.; Changes operand matching and constant-splat use within an existing X86 combine routine.; Adds extensive llvm/test/CodeGen/X86 GFNI folding coverage across AVX and AVX-512 vector widths.; The added tests do not cover the reported low-bits width-adjustment assertion path.

For a constant GFNI affine matrix, it folds the XOR into a replacement GF2P8AFFINEQB whose matrix rows are XORed with the byte identity matrix; it also renames the matched XOR operand from SplatOp to XorOp and retains the existing constant-splat folding path using that operand.
behavioral_change: Adds a fold from GF2P8AFFINEQB(x, M, Imm) ^ x to GF2P8AFFINEQB(x, M ^ IDENTITY, Imm) when the affine matrix can be extracted as constant 8-bit element values.
Builds a new vector matrix by XORing each extracted matrix row with the repeating identity rows {128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1}.
Uses XorOp, rather than the former SplatOp name, as the non-GFNI XOR operand for both source-XOR recognition and the existing constant-splat check.

Adds X86 GFNI tests for 128-, 256-, and 512-bit source-XOR folding, including non-splat matrices, nonzero immediates, multi-use no-fold cases, variable matrices, and unrelated-variable XOR no-fold cases.

However, the changed transform is narrowly for GF2P8AFFINEQB vector-i8 affine operations and source XORs. Adds extensive llvm/test/CodeGen/X86 GFNI folding coverage across AVX and AVX-512 vector widths.
The added tests do not cover the reported low-bits width-adjustment assertion path.

diff --git a/llvm/docs/AMDGPUUsage.rst b/llvm/docs/AMDGPUUsage.rst
index 8dd743a995a9..61841716792e 100644
--- a/llvm/docs/AMDGPUUsage.rst
+++ b/llvm/docs/AMDGPUUsage.rst
@@ -832,0 +833,49 @@ For example:
+.. _amdgpu-module-flags:
+
+Module Flags
+------------
+
+AMDGPU-specific behaviour can be controlled via LLVM module flags (see
+`Module Flags Metadata
+<https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#module-flags-metadata>`_ in the language
+reference). These flags are set by frontends and are
+consumed by the AMDGPU backend during code generation.
+
+.. list-table:: AMDGPU Module Flags
+   :name: amdgpu-module-flags-table
+   :header-rows: 1
+
+   * - Flag Name
+     - Type
+     - Merge
+     - Description
+   * - ``amdgpu.buffer.oob.mode``
+     - ``i32``
+     - Max
+     - Controls out-of-bounds semantics for untyped buffer
+       instructions (``buffer_load`` / ``buffer_store``).
+
+       - ``0`` (or absent): **any**. The module does not care about OOB
+         semantics. This is an alias of **strict** that is allowed to link
+         with any other module. Code generation is identical to **strict**.
+       - ``1``: **relaxed**. The backend may merge misaligned buffer
+         accesses for performance, even if that changes OOB behaviour.
+       - ``2``: **strict**. The backend preserves per-byte OOB guarantees
+         by preventing merging of misaligned buffer accesses that could
+         straddle an OOB boundary (e.g. as required by Vulkan
+         ``robustBufferAccess2``).
+
+   * - ``amdgpu.tbuffer.oob.mode``
+     - ``i32``
+     - Max
+     - Same as above, but for typed buffer instructions (``tbuffer_load`` /
+       ``tbuffer_store``).
+
+.. note::
+
+   Frontends that require misaligned-access merging for performance should
+   set both flags to ``1`` (relaxed).  Frontends that require strict
+   per-byte OOB guarantees should set the flags to ``2`` (strict) as needed.
+   Modules that do not use buffer operations or are indifferent to OOB semantics
+   (e.g. device libraries) should leave the flags absent.
+

top_candidates.subject: [X86] lowerShuffleAsBitMask - use getConstVector to create bitmask (#200889)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Changes X86 shuffle lowering so lowerShuffleAsBitMask constructs an integer-typed constant mask directly with getConstVector, rather than building a mask in the original/floating-point vector type and bitcasting it to an integer logic type. It removes the Subtarget-dependent i64-to-f64 workaround for 32-bit targets and updates all shown shuffle-lowering callers to the simplified helper signature.
Changed symbols: lowerShuffleAsBitMask; lowerV4I32Shuffle; lowerV8I16Shuffle; lowerV16I8Shuffle; lowerV64I8Shuffle; lower512BitShuffle; lowerShuffleAsBlend
Behavioral change: Creates zero and all-ones mask elements as APInt values sized from VT.getScalarSizeInBits().; Constructs the shuffle bitmask directly as an integer vector through getConstVector instead of getBuildVector followed by getBitcast.; Removes the special 32-bit-target path that represented i64 mask elements as f64 before bitcasting.; Changes the DAG value types and node construction sequence used for bitmask-based X86 shuffle lowering.
Assertion or trace link: X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG; integer width adjustment
Reproducer link: No retrieved hunk identifies the reduced C testcase as containing a vector shuffle or invoking lowerShuffleAsBitMask.; No retrieved hunk mentions an O1 crash or the reported assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 SelectionDAG lowering; X86 shuffle lowering
Causal explanation: This is the strongest candidate of the three because it changes X86 SelectionDAG construction in X86ISelLowering.cpp and directly changes how integer-width mask constants are represented, including removal of a width/type workaround. Such changed DAG typing could affect later combines. However, the retrieved code is specific to vector-shuffle bitmask lowering and contains no direct reference to peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, combineBTToBitOpFlag, low-bits constraints, bit tests, or sign/zero-extension reasoning, so the causal connection to the reported assertion is indirect.
Causal confidence: 0.26
Build risk: The helper signature drops the X86Subtarget parameter, and all retrieved callers were updated accordingly.; The removed f64 fallback changes behavior for i64-element masks on non-64-bit targets.; No test changes are visible in the retrieved hunks, so regression coverage for the revised mask construction is not evidenced here.

top_candidates.subject: [SelectionDAG] Widen <2 x T> vector types for atomic store (#197618)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Adds SelectionDAG vector-type-legalization support for atomic stores whose vector value must be widened, coercing the widened value back to a legal memory-width representation and emitting a single ATOMIC_STORE. The change wires the new handler into WidenVectorOperand and adds X86 atomic-vector-store coverage.
Changed symbols: coerceStoredValue; DAGTypeLegalizer::WidenVecOp_ATOMIC_STORE; DAGTypeLegalizer::WidenVectorOperand; DAGTypeLegalizer
Behavioral change: Adds inverse coercion of a widened stored value by bitcasting to a vector of the original scalar type and extracting element zero when the original memory type is scalar.; Finds a memory type matching the original atomic-store width without allowing alignment to widen the access beyond the object.; Creates an ATOMIC_STORE with the recovered memory type and coerced value when widening a vector operand.; Routes ISD::ATOMIC_STORE through the new vector-widening legalization handler.
Assertion or trace link: SelectionDAG; width adjustment
Reproducer link: The added tests cover atomic stores of small vectors such as <2 x i8>, <2 x i16>, and <2 x i32>.; The issue context does not state that the crashing reduced C testcase contains atomic operations or vector atomic stores.; No retrieved hunk mentions the low-bits assertion, peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, or combineBTToBitOpFlag.
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG type legalization; atomic-store vector widening
Causal explanation: The commit operates in SelectionDAG and explicitly performs width-sensitive bitcasts and extraction while legalizing widened values, which gives it a superficial connection to the issue's width-adjustment theme. Its scope is nevertheless restricted to atomic stores, whereas the reported trace identifies an X86 DAG combine/bit-test path. The available evidence does not connect the reproducer to atomic vector-store legalization.

Its new wrapper-peeling logic performs the width adjustment immediately preceding that assertion, so an input whose bit-position width becomes smaller than log2(BW) can trigger the reported failure during the newly added BT-to-bit-operation fusion.

build_risk: Adds a substantial X86 CodeGen regression test file covering mask and extension peel-through cases on x86_64 and i686.
Updates existing X86 big-integer bit-test code-generation expectations to use BTR/BTS/BTC flag-producing instructions.
Introduces new TableGen DAG nodes and patterns plus a new X86 DAG combine, increasing target-selection and assertion exposure.
No build or test execution result is supplied in the retrieved evidence.

+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_llc_test_checks.py
+; RUN: llc < %s -mtriple=x86_64-- | FileCheck %s --check-prefixes=CHECK,X64
+; RUN: llc < %s -mtriple=i686-- | FileCheck %s --check-prefixes=CHECK,X86
+
+; Pin the peek-through paths in combineBTToBitOpFlag: the bit positions of
+; BT and the bit-modify can differ by an (and x, BW-1) mask or by trunc/zext
+; wrappers, and the combine should still fuse them into a single BTR/BTS/BTC.
+
+; (and x, 31) on the modify side, bare on the BT side.
+define i1 @fuse_and_mask_on_modify(ptr %word, i32 %position) nounwind {
+; X64-LABEL: fuse_and_mask_on_modify:
+; X64:       # %bb.0:
+; X64-NEXT:    movl (%rdi), %ecx
+; X64-NEXT:    btcl %esi, %ecx
+; X64-NEXT:    setb %al
+; X64-NEXT:    movl %ecx, (%rdi)
+; X64-NEXT:    retq
+;
+; X86-LABEL: fuse_and_mask_on_modify:
+; X86:       # %bb.0:
+; X86-NEXT:    movl {{[0-9]+}}(%esp), %ecx
+; X86-NEXT:    movl (%ecx), %edx
+; X86-NEXT:    movl {{[0-9]+}}(%esp), %eax
+; X86-NEXT:    btcl %eax, %edx
+; X86-NEXT:    setb %al
+; X86-NEXT:    movl %edx, (%ecx)
+; X86-NEXT:    retl
+  %ofs = and i32 %position, 31
+  %bit = shl i32 1, %ofs
+  %ld = load i32, ptr %word
+  %res = xor i32 %ld, %bit
+  %test = and i32 %ld, %bit
+  %cmp = icmp ne i32 %test, 0
+  store i32 %res, ptr %word
+  ret i1 %cmp
+}
+
+; (and x, 63) on the BT side, bare on the modify side.

+; X64-NEXT:    setb %al
+; X64-NEXT:    movq %rcx, (%rdi)
+; X64-NEXT:    retq
+;
+; X86-LABEL: fuse_and_mask_on_bt:
+; X86:       # %bb.0:
+; X86-NEXT:    pushl %edi
+; X86-NEXT:    pushl %esi
+; X86-NEXT:    movl {{[0-9]+}}(%esp), %edx
+; X86-NEXT:    movl {{[0-9]+}}(%esp), %ecx

+; X86-NEXT:  # %bb.1:
+; X86-NEXT:    movl %esi, %edi
+; X86-NEXT:    xorl %esi, %esi
+; X86-NEXT:  .LBB1_2:
+; X86-NEXT:    movl %ecx, %eax
+; X86-NEXT:    andl $32, %eax
+; X86-NEXT:    shrl $3, %eax
+; X86-NEXT:    movl (%edx,%eax), %eax
+; X86-NEXT:    btl %ecx, %eax
+; X86-NEXT:    setb %al
+; X86-NEXT:    orl %esi, (%edx)
+; X86-NEXT:    orl %edi, 4(%edx)

+  store i64 %res, ptr %word

+}

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Changes the X86 DAG combine for ORs involving GF2P8AFFINEQB. Instead of only folding a disjoint OR by XORing the immediate, it recognizes a one-use GF2P8AFFINEQB ORed with a constant byte splat; disjoint cases retain the immediate-XOR fold, while general constant-splat ORs are folded by clearing affected affine-matrix rows and ORing the forced output bits into the instruction immediate.
Changed symbols: combineOrWithGF2P8AFFINEQB; combineAddOrSubToADCOrSBB; X86::isConstantSplat; getTargetConstantBitsFromNode

top_candidates.subject: [X86] Move Non-VLX handling for VPMADD52 instructions entirely into tablegen (#200800)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This X86 change moves non-VLX support for narrow VPMADD52 operations from runtime SelectionDAG-combine legality checks into TableGen patterns. The combine path now treats v2i64 and v4i64 PMADD52 operations as supported with IFMA or AVXIFMA, while new HasIFMA/NoVLX patterns implement narrow operands by inserting them into 512-bit vectors, issuing a 512-bit VPMADD52 instruction, and extracting the narrow subregister result.
Changed symbols: combineMulToPMADD52; matchVPMADD52; VPMADD52LUQ; VPMADD52HUQ; avx512_pmadd52_common
Behavioral change: combineMulToPMADD52 broadens the small-vector support predicate from requiring IFMA plus VLX, or AVXIFMA, to requiring IFMA or AVXIFMA.; matchVPMADD52 no longer contains its runtime rejection for sub-512-bit operations when the prior feature condition is not met.; For HasIFMA and NoVLX, TableGen patterns lower v2i64/v4i64 PMADD52 DAG nodes through 512-bit VPMADD52 instructions with INSERT_SUBREG, IMPLICIT_DEF, and EXTRACT_SUBREG.
Assertion or trace link: X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG
Reproducer link: No reduced C reproducer, -O1-specific behavior, low-bits assertion, or crash diagnostic is present in the retrieved hunks.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 SelectionDAG lowering and combining; X86 TableGen instruction selection
Causal explanation: This is a direct X86 SelectionDAG-lowering change and can create different DAG shapes and subregister/width transitions for PMADD52 operations, which is generally adjacent to the reported width-adjustment assertion. However, its affected operations are AVX-512 IFMA VPMADD52 vector patterns, whereas the trace identifies low-bit preservation in peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc and combineBTToBitOpFlag. No retrieved hunk touches those functions, BT/bit-test lowering, or their low-bit constraint logic. Thus the subsystem overlap is real but the operation-specific causal evidence is limited.
Causal confidence: 0.14
Build risk: The implementation moves legality/selection responsibility across C++ DAG-combine code and TableGen patterns, so feature predicates and pattern coverage must remain consistent.; The new patterns depend on correct 128/256-to-512 subregister insertion and extraction semantics under HasIFMA and NoVLX.; No X86 test hunk is included in the retrieved evidence for the new non-VLX PMADD52 lowering paths.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Changes X86 lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB to build PSHUFB shuffle masks as integer lane values and materialize them through getConstVector rather than constructing an SDValue build-vector from per-lane constants or undef nodes. The change also updates AVX-512 shuffle tests to expect a reusable broadcast constant mask followed by PSHUFB instructions.
Changed symbols: lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB; getConstVector; shuffle_v64i8_to_v32i8; shuffle_v64i8_to_v32i8_1
Behavioral change: Represents the PSHUFB mask initially as SmallVector<int> with -1 for undef lanes rather than SmallVector<SDValue> containing DAG constants and DAG undef values.; Uses getConstVector(..., IsMask=true) to materialize the vector mask before forming X86ISD::PSHUFB.; Preserves the PSHUFB zeroing encoding by using integer mask byte 0x80 for lanes that must zero.; Changes expected AVX512VL code generation from embedded/printed shuffle masks to a vpbroadcastq-produced mask register reused by vpshufb.
Assertion or trace link: X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG
Reproducer link: The retrieved tests exercise vector byte-shuffle lowering on AVX-512 targets, not the reduced scalar C testcase or an -O1 assertion involving a BT bit-position value.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 SelectionDAG lowering; PSHUFB vector-shuffle lowering
Causal explanation: This candidate is in the same X86 SelectionDAG lowering implementation named by the issue and changes DAG construction, so it has a weak subsystem-level connection. However, its only visible functional target is vector PSHUFB mask construction; it does not touch BT, BTR/BTS/BTC fusion, peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, low-bit constraints, or integer extension/truncation reasoning for bit positions. The retrieved evidence therefore does not support it as the direct cause of the reported assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.04

Summary: Changes the X86 SelectionDAG combine for OR expressions around GF2P8AFFINEQB. It retains the existing disjoint-OR immediate-XOR fold, but adds a more general fold for an OR with a constant byte splat by rewriting the affine matrix rows for masked output bits and OR-ing the mask into the instruction immediate. It also adds X86 GFNI code-generation tests for 128-, 256-, and 512-bit vectors.
Changed symbols: combineOrWithGF2P8AFFINEQB; X86ISD::GF2P8AFFINEQB; X86::isConstantSplat; getTargetConstantBitsFromNode; test_or_disjoint_overlap_with_imm; test_affine_or_fold_v16i8; test_affine_or_fold_v16i8_mask33; test_affine_or_fold_v32i8
Behavioral change: The combine now first matches a one-use GF2P8AFFINEQB result OR-ed with a fully defined constant splat, rather than requiring the entire fold to be proven disjoint before matching.; For disjoint operands or operands proven to have no common set bits, it preserves the prior transformation that XORs the splat value into the GFNI immediate.; For a general constant-splat OR, it constructs a replacement constant matrix: every matrix row corresponding to a mask-selected output bit is cleared, while the same mask bits are OR-ed into the GFNI immediate. This makes those output bits constant one without requiring the original affine output to be disjoint from the mask.; The new path is restricted to GF2P8AFFINEQB with a constant, non-undef matrix and a constant byte splat.

Summary: Moves X86 non-VLX handling for narrow VPMADD52 operations from X86ISelLowering legality checks into TableGen patterns. top_candidates.subject: [SelectionDAG] Don't over-claim alignment on vector splice/compress stack MMOs (#200622)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Corrects SelectionDAG stack memory operands created while expanding vector splice and VECTOR_COMPRESS operations so that their explicit load/store alignment matches the reduced alignment used when allocating the stack temporary. The change records the temporary's alignment in a local variable and passes it through to the corresponding stores, loads, and stack pointer metadata.
Changed symbols: TargetLowering::expandVectorSplice; TargetLowering::expandVECTOR_COMPRESS
Behavioral change: Stack stores generated by expandVectorSplice now carry the stack temporary's explicit reduced alignment.; The temporary stack pointer metadata for vector splice now records that same alignment.; VECTOR_COMPRESS expansion now uses one recorded Alignment value both for stack-temporary creation and for its generated passthrough store and result load.; The effective invariant is that generated memory operands no longer imply a stronger alignment than the stack temporary actually has.
Assertion or trace link: SelectionDAG
Reproducer link: No retrieved hunk links the reported -O1 X86 crash to vector splice, VECTOR_COMPRESS, stack temporaries, or memory alignment.
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG TargetLowering expansion; vector splice expansion; VECTOR_COMPRESS expansion
Causal explanation: The commit is in the broader SelectionDAG subsystem, but its visible effect is limited to alignment metadata on stack loads and stores emitted for vector splice/compress expansion. It does not touch X86-specific lowering, DAG combines, bit-test lowering, extension/truncation reasoning, or the low-bits constraint assertion path. The available evidence therefore provides no substantive mechanism connecting this alignment fix to the reported assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.03
Build risk: Changes explicit MachineMemOperand alignment on generated stack loads and stores, which can affect legality decisions and target instruction selection.; The patch centralizes use of the Alignment returned by getReducedAlign, reducing mismatch risk between stack allocation and generated memory operations.; Retrieved coverage is truncated and contains no visible test hunks, so test evidence for the alignment correction is unavailable in the provided material.

Summary: Adds an X86 SelectionDAG combine that fuses an X86ISD::BT bit test with a sibling matching bit-clear, bit-set, or bit-toggle operation into a flag-producing X86ISD::BTR, X86ISD::BTS, or X86ISD::BTC node. The combine reasons through truncate, zero/any-extend, and low-bit-preserving AND wrappers around bit positions, adds matching TableGen patterns, and introduces extensive X86 code-generation coverage.

Behavioral change: Adds peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc to strip TRUNCATE, ZERO_EXTEND, ANY_EXTEND, and AND-mask wrappers from a BT bit-position expression when the mask retains the low log2(source-width) bits used by x86 bit-test instructions.; Adds an invariant assertion after traversing width-adjustment nodes: the underlying value must retain at least log2(BW) bits, reported as "low bits constraint must survive width adjustment".; Fuses BT with matching sibling AND/rotate-mask, OR/shift-one, or XOR/shift-one bit modifications when their bit positions are equivalent after wrapper peeling.; Creates flag-producing BTR/BTS/BTC DAG nodes whose carry flag replaces the separate BT result, then selects ordinary BTR/BTS/BTC register forms for i32 and i64 operands.; Adds tests specifically exercising AND masks and zero-extension/truncation wrappers on bit positions and checking fused btr/bts/btc output.

+define i1 @fuse_and_mask_on_modify(ptr %word, i32 %position) nounwind {

+; X64:       # %bb.0:

+  %res = xor i32 %ld, %bit
+  %test = and i32 %ld, %bit
+  %cmp = icmp ne i32 %test, 0

+; X64-NEXT:    movq %rcx, (%rdi)
+; X64-NEXT:    retq

+; X86:       # %bb.0:
+; X86-NEXT:    pushl %edi
+; X86-NEXT:    pushl %esi
+; X86-NEXT:    movl {{[0-9]+}}(%esp), %edx
+; X86-NEXT:    movl {{[0-9]+}}(%esp), %ecx

+; Check that convert_ builtins pick the signed/unsigned opcode from the source
+; operand signedness.
+
+; RUN: llc -O0 -mtriple=spirv32-unknown-unknown %s -o - | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: %if spirv-tools %{ llc -O0 -mtriple=spirv32-unknown-unknown %s -o - -filetype=obj | spirv-val %}
+
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#StoS:]] "s_to_s"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#StoU:]] "s_to_u"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#UtoS:]] "u_to_s"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#UtoU:]] "u_to_u"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#StoF:]] "s_to_f"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#UtoF:]] "u_to_f"
+
+; signed source -> signed dest: sign-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#StoS]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpSConvert
+define spir_func void @s_to_s(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z12convert_longi(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; signed source -> unsigned dest: sign-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#StoU]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpSConvert
+define spir_func void @s_to_u(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z13convert_ulongi(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; unsigned source -> signed dest: zero-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#UtoS]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpUConvert
+define spir_func void @u_to_s(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z12convert_longj(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; unsigned source -> unsigned dest: zero-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#UtoU]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpUConvert
+define spir_func void @u_to_u(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z13convert_ulongj(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; signed source -> float.
+; CHECK: %[[#StoF]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpConvertSToF
+define spir_func void @s_to_f(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func float @_Z13convert_floati(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; unsigned source -> float.
+; CHECK: %[[#UtoF]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpConvertUToF
+define spir_func void @u_to_f(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func float @_Z13convert_floatj(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+declare spir_func i64 @_Z12convert_longi(i32 noundef)
+declare spir_func i64 @_Z13convert_ulongi(i32 noundef)
+declare spir_func i64 @_Z12convert_longj(i32 noundef)
+declare spir_func i64 @_Z13convert_ulongj(i32 noundef)
+declare spir_func float @_Z13convert_floati(i32 noundef)
+declare spir_func float @_Z13convert_floatj(i32 noundef)
